title: How Sagebrush is built
about: The architecture, with a tour: where it runs, the notebook, the compiler, the runtime, the library and the engines.

title: Three proofs that there are infinitely many primes
about: Euclid, Euler and Fürstenberg, a page each, with tours: pages, math, and printing (or saving as PDF) a sheet per page or per step.

title: The Collatz map, live
about: Code items: Python on one interpreter for the board, run reactively in reading order, their output under their code. Double-click one to change it (Shift+Enter runs it).

title: Mermaid flowcharts, laid out by the board
about: Markdown with two Mermaid diagrams, a page each: a cell running, every shape and kind of line; and Mermaid's own code flow, about 100 nodes. Open your own .mmd file or paste one.

title: What does transitive mean?
about: A lesson in Sage on permutation groups: orbits, the orbit-stabilizer theorem, blocks and primitive groups, with questions that check their answers, hints that grow, and a question in your own words.

title: Sagebrush's source, file by file
about: About 300 source files with their opening comments and links to GitHub; directories as groups, imports as edges. Generated from the repository.

title: The integers to 10,000
about: 10,000 notes with factorizations and arithmetic functions in LaTeX: how a large board feels.
